root_cause.text: The driver was using `urb->transfer_buffer_length` (the maximum buffer size allocated by the driver) instead of `urb->actual_length` (the actual size of data received) when validating message boundaries during USB bulk transfer parsing, allowing out-of-bounds buffer reads.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly changes the length validation check from `if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)` to `if (start > urb->actual_length)` and adds a new pre-parsing check `if (start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN > urb->actual_length)`. The commit message clarifies that "actual_length is the size of the buffer passed to the driver, not the transfer_buffer_length which is set by the driver as the max size of the buffer," indicating the original code was comparing against the wrong field, enabling potential buffer overflow when parsing multiple CAN messages in a single USB transfer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add bounds checking to prevent out-of-bounds buffer access when parsing CPC messages from USB bulk transfers.
intent_record.what: Added a bounds check before dereferencing the message buffer. The code now validates that `start + CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN` does not exceed `urb->actual_length` before accessing `ibuf[start]` as a message structure.
intent_record.how: This prevents out-of-bounds memory access when processing USB bulk transfer data. If the remaining buffer is too small to contain a complete message header, the loop breaks early and logs an error instead of reading past the valid data region.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix USB message parsing validation to check against actual received data length instead of buffer capacity.
intent_record.what: Changed the boundary check condition from comparing `start` against `urb->transfer_buffer_length` to comparing it against `urb->actual_length`.
intent_record.how: This fixes the validation logic to check against the actual amount of data received in the URB transfer rather than the allocated buffer size. The `actual_length` field contains the true number of bytes transferred by the device, while `transfer_buffer_length` is the pre-allocated buffer capacity. Using `actual_length` prevents false positives when the device sends less data than the buffer can hold, and correctly detects format errors based on what was actually received.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable code is present in the `ems_usb_read_bulk_callback` function. At line 'if (start > urb->transfer_buffer_length)', the code uses `urb->transfer_buffer_length` (the maximum allocated buffer size) instead of `urb->actual_length` (the actual size of data received from the USB device). This allows the message parsing loop to read beyond the actual received data boundaries. The loop processes messages by incrementing `start += CPC_MSG_HEADER_LEN + msg->length` and only validates against the allocated buffer size, not the actual received data size. This creates an out-of-bounds read vulnerability where uninitialized or stale buffer data could be interpreted as valid CAN messages. The fix would require changing the boundary check to use `urb->actual_length` instead of `urb->transfer_buffer_length`.
